entries.title: Proverbs 24:2
segments:
CHAP. XXIV. 
 
  V. 2. Destruction-How they may oppress and destroy others.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:3
segments: V. 3. Through wisdom-There is no need that thou shouldest raise thy family by ruining others, which thou mayest more effectually do by wisdom.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:4
segments: V. 4. By knowledge-Which in scripture phrase includes the love and practice of what we know.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:5
segments: V. 5. Is strong-Is courageous and resolute, and able by wisdom to do greater things than others can accomplish by strength.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:6
segments: V. 6. Thy war-War is better managed by wisdom than by strength.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:7
segments: V. 7. A fool-For a wicked man, whose sins enfeeble his mind, and make it incapable of wisdom.  Openeth not-He knows not how to speak acceptably, and profitably in the publick assembly.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:8
segments: V. 8. Shall be called-Though he cover his wicked devices with fair pretences, he shall be branded with that infamy which is due to him.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:9
segments: V. 9. The thought-The very inward thought or contrivance of evil, is a sin in God's sight.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:11
segments: V. 11. Deliver-When it is in thy power.  Drawn-By the violence of lawless men.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:12
segments: V. 12. Consider-That this is only a frivolous excuse.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:13
segments: V. 13. Eat-This is not a command, but a concession, and is only here expressed to illustrate the following verse.  Honey in those parts was an usual food.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:14
segments: V. 14. A reward-It is not only sweet for the present, but brings a sure and everlasting reward.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:16
segments: V. 16. Falleth-Into calamities, of which he evidently speaks both in the foregoing verse, and in the following branch of this verse. Fall-Frequently into irrecoverable destruction.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:17
segments: V. 17. Falleth-Into mischief.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:18
segments: V. 18. From him-Understand, upon thee, which is implied in the Hebrew phrase.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:20
segments: V. 20. No reward-All his happiness shall quickly and eternally perish. The candle-All their comfort and glory shall cease.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:21
segments: V. 21. To change-That are unstable in their obedience to God or to the king.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:22
segments: V. 22. Who knoweth-Who can conceive how sore and sudden will be the ruin of them that fear not God, and the king.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:23
segments: V. 23. These-The counsels following, to the end of the chapter, no less than those hitherto mentioned, are worthy of their consideration.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:25
segments: V. 25. Rebuke-That publickly and judicially rebuke and condemn the wicked.  Delight-The peace of a good conscience.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:26
segments: V. 26. Shall kiss-Shall respect him.  A right answer-That speaks pertinently and plainly, and truly.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:32
segments: V. 32. Received-I learned wisdom by his folly.
